summary: This Dockerfile builds a development container for Quarto documentation with optional tools. It starts from a pre-built Quarto image, installs system dependencies and PDF rendering libraries, then optionally adds spell-checking and code-quality tools. Finally, it creates a non-root user with custom shell aliases and a welcome message.

explanations.1: This tells Docker to use a newer syntax version that enables better caching features (the --mount flags used later).
explanations.4: We're starting from an existing Quarto image rather than a bare OS, so we skip building Quarto ourselves.
explanations.6: These ARG lines define build-time arguments that can be passed in when building, with sensible defaults like username 'vscode'.
explanations.10: These boolean arguments let you optionally skip installing Chromium, spell-checker, and pre-commit hooks to keep the image smaller.
explanations.17: Setting LANG and LC_ALL ensures the container uses UTF-8 encoding for all text, avoiding encoding issues.
explanations.24: The --mount flags cache apt packages between builds so we don't re-download them; 'set -eux' makes the script fail fast on errors.
explanations.28: We install many small packages with one apt-get call rather than many separate calls, which is more efficient in Docker.
explanations.56: Similar to line 24, we cache the yq download so future builds don't re-fetch it.
explanations.64: We're creating a second stage called 'extras' that builds on 'base'; this lets us keep a lean base without optional tools.
explanations.71: The cache mount here persists pip's cache between builds; the conditional checks if pre-commit should be installed at all.
explanations.85: We cache npm's package cache in the user's home directory; '${USERNAME}' gets substituted with the actual username.
explanations.99: The 'final' stage starts from 'extras', so it includes everything from all previous stages.
explanations.107: We create a user account instead of running as root for security; this is standard practice in dev containers.
explanations.121: We switch to running as the non-root user for all subsequent commands.
explanations.124: The cache mount here stores Quarto's downloaded tools so they're not re-downloaded if the image is rebuilt.
explanations.135: We're creating shell aliases that get printed every time the user opens a bash session, making commands easier to remember.
explanations.141: These lines configure bash history to persist across sessions and store more entries (10,000 instead of the default).
explanations.167: This checks if optional tools were installed, and if so, adds a section to the welcome message telling users how to use them.
